newsitem.title: MALAWI: MALAWI PLANS NEW ANTI-CORRUPTION CODE ON CONTRACTS.
newsitem.headline: MALAWI PLANS NEW ANTI-CORRUPTION CODE ON CONTRACTS.

text.p: Malawian President Bakili Muluzi said on Tuesday his government would revise its procurement code for the award of international contracts to boost his country's fight against corruption.
Muluzi said in a statement the action would be taken as part of a strengthening of Malawi's integrity.

"Corrupt practises will be taken to mean the soliciting or receiving, as well as the offering or giving, of value designed to influence actions in the process of procurement or execution or executions of contracts," the president said.
The statement did not elaborate on the measures nor when they would come into effect.
Malawi's Anti-Corruption Bureau director, Gilton Chiwaula, told Reuters the statement was signal that the government was determined to enforce standards.
"Standards will be set and people will be expected to meet those standards. There should be integrity so that the public should benefit," he said.
The minimum penalty for corruption in Malawi is a non-optional fine of K50,000 ($2,900) and a prison sentence of between five and 12 years.
